item.title: Charvarius Ward Makes Hilarious Comment Explaining Why Lions Won’t Trade for Him
item.description: The Detroit Lions have been connected to Indianapolis Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, but the veteran defensive back doesn’t seem too concerned about being dealt. In fact, Ward offered a pretty hilarious explanation for why he thinks the Lions, or any other team, might hesitate to acquire him. According to Colts beat reporter James Boyd , Ward was asked on Monday about the possibility of being traded. The former Pro Bowl cornerback acknowledged that teams could be interested in acquiring his services before pointing out one rather expensive obstacle. “If you’re a good player and you feel like you got a little value … teams might be interested in you. If a team needs a corner, I don’t know if they’re gonna look for Mooney. Mooney making $20 million a year.” At least Ward is self-aware! Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Indianapolis Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward (7) tackles Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) during the first half at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Have Reportedly Called About Charvarius Ward Ward’s comments are particularly interesting considering A to Z Sports reported that the Lions have already contacted Indianapolis about the veteran cornerback. There is no indication Detroit has made an offer, but general manager Brad Holmes is clearly exploring his options. The Lions have already acquired veteran safety Andre Cisco , and adding a proven outside cornerback could further strengthen their defense. However, with Detroit already facing some important roster decisions in the secondary , Ward’s contract is certainly something Holmes would need to consider. According to the Indianapolis Star , Ward is under contract through 2027 and carries a cap hit of approximately $19.9 million this season with Indianapolis. Ward also indicated that he’s happy with the Colts and hopes to remain there. Whether the Lions ultimately make a move for Ward remains to be seen. But you have to appreciate a player who can laugh about making $20 million a year while explaining why nobody might want to trade for him. Mooney has a pretty good problem to have.

Now, Porter is going to therapy for his gambling problem, as he told The New Yorker. Hopefully, he is getting the treatment he needs. item.title: Mavericks' Kyrie Irving gets major trade update as future with Dallas remains in question
item.description: Mavericks' Kyrie Irving gets major trade update as future with Dallas remains in question originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks have some interesting decisions to make as the trade deadline approaches. Ever since the offseason, there have been a few names that could potentially be on the move. Dallas is 7-4 in a crowded Western Conference, where winning games on a nightly basis will be a challenge. Kyrie Irving has been vocal about focusing on what is in front of the team and continuing to build alongside Cooper Flagg. “We are still growing," Irving said. "We still have a level we want to get to — a higher level. We are going to continue to push each other. We obviously know the external chatter as well and the 15-year age gap and what we are going to accomplish and how we are going to mesh. I think we threw all that out the window and just really focused on what we can control, which is our effort and how we treat each other." Irving's future in Dallas remains uncertain. One thing is for certain: he could be one of the biggest names available on the trade market. “I think he’s going to be the most in-demand player at the trade deadline because he’s not on the Mavericks’ timeline. And we talked about Houston. I think Detroit’s another team that will be salivating over getting Kyrie Irving,” Sports Illustrated’s Chris Mannix said. However, ESPN's Brian Windhorst believes that the injuries piling up across the Western Conference could change Dallas' plans and give the Mavericks a reason to hold onto Irving for a potential playoff run. “Dallas is a team that you know, again, at the start of the season you’re like, when/ if they’re trading Kyrie? Now, you look at what’s happened to the West, Minnesota injuries, Oklahoma City injuries, you’re like, uh I don’t know,” Windhorst said. Keeping Irving in Dallas as a mentor for the younger players wouldn't be the worst outcome, especially considering the value he brings both on and off the court. The Mavericks would like to keep him around for as long as possible. However, another team could make an offer that Dallas simply cannot turn down. Only time will tell. The Mavericks will likely continue evaluating the situation throughout the first half of the season before making a final decision. item.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. item.title: Bournemouth star receives first England call-up
item.description: Bournemouth star receives first England call-up James Hill Earns First England Call-Up as England Need Defensive Cover England have made a simple, sensible decision. James Hill is in, Ezri Konsa is out for Thursday, and Thomas Tuchel needs cover at centre-back before the Nations League meeting with Croatia at Wembley. Hill, 24, receives his first senior England call-up after a season built on availability and consistency. That matters. He has played every minute of Bournemouth’s Premier League campaign and has also featured in every match of their first Europa League run. Managers notice that. So do international coaches. England Turn to James Hill Konsa’s issue is a knee injury, suffered in the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. He was taken off in that match, although the timeline around his fitness has not been straightforward given he then completed 90 minutes in the win over Hull on Saturday. The expectation is that he will return to full training this week, ahead of England’s game against Spain in Madrid on Sunday. Photo IMAGO For now, though, he is unavailable for Croatia, and Hill gets his chance. Bournemouth Form Drives Selection This call-up has not come from nowhere. Hill joined Bournemouth from Fleetwood in January 2022 for an undisclosed fee, and for a long period he was a squad player, making only 24 appearances across his first three and a half years at the club. That has changed. Last season he became a regular as Bournemouth recorded their highest top-flight finish of sixth. This season he has gone further, staying ever-present while Bournemouth put together an eight-match winning run in all competitions and sit seventh in the Premier League. Defensive Depth Tested Before Croatia England’s defensive reshuffle had already started before Hill’s inclusion. On Sunday, Dan Burn replaced Marc Guehi after the Man City defender withdrew with a hip injury. Tuchel now has another option, and Hill has earned it the hard way, by playing, by staying fit, and by doing his job every week. There is no romance in that, only logic. England needed cover, and James Hill has given them a reason to trust him.

item.title: Why ESPN’s nearly $1.7 billion CFP deal costs the network less than it seems
item.description: ESPN will remain the sole rights holder of the College Football Playoff when the bracket doubles to 24 teams in 2027, under a five-year deal worth nearly $1.7 billion, sources told ESPN’s Heather Dinich . The CFP made the expansion official Monday, and the new terms run through the 2031-32 season. The field will include the four Power 4 champions, the highest-ranked Group of 6 team and 19 at-large selections. The top eight seeds get byes, the first two rounds are played on campus, and the New Year’s Six bowls keep the quarterfinals and semifinals. The selection committee will keep ranking 25 teams each week and could stretch that list to 30 to show which teams sit on the bubble. The national championship game is set for Jan. 24, 2028, in New Orleans. The College Football Playoff logo is painted in the endzone prior to the Cotton Bowl between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Miami Hurricanes at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas on Dec. 31, 2025. ESPN’s added payment averages $345 million a year on top of the roughly $1.3 billion it already pays annually, sources told ESPN’s Pete Thamel . About $140 million of that comes back to the network each year, because the SEC, Big 12 and ACC championship games it holds the rights to will no longer be played. That puts ESPN’s real increase near $205 million a year. Fox, which televises the Big Ten title game, is expected to recoup about $50 million annually. Spread across the 12 new playoff games, ESPN’s net figure comes to roughly $17 million a game, and the network can sublicense six of those games to approved partners. It already sublicenses part of the 12-team bracket to TNT Sports. Combined, the two networks’ recoveries come to about $190 million, so more than half of the new annual payment covers rights fees the leagues were already collecting for their own title games. The ticket, sponsorship and game-day revenue from those events disappears as well. item.description: Kayden Delamere admitted she still is in pain and can’t run at full speed, and she likely will need an MRI to determine the extent of the damage to her ailing knee. It’s one of the reasons tears streamed down her face last Saturday, during one of the proudest moments she has experienced in soccer. “When we won last year, I was just happy,” the Kennedy Catholic senior said. “This time, I was emotional because it felt like we really earned something.” The Gaels had what coach Gareth Horrocks called a “unicorn season” last fall, having everything fall into place to go undefeated. But this run for them was even more fulfilling because it wasn’t perfect, it wasn’t a certainty, and it required even more. So, as Delamere ate with the team afterwards, celebrating fittingly with Buffalo wings, her swollen knee told the tale of sacrifice and triumph against adversity. Kennedy Catholic rallied for a 2-1 victory over Mount Mercy Academy, winning a second straight CHSAA Class A state championship at St. Joseph's Collegiate Institute in Buffalo. Stella Sullivan scored twice, including the winner with 3:07 remaining. Emelia Delamere dribbled through a crowd inside the 30 then lofted a pass ahead to Sullivan on the right. In a spectacular sequence, the sophomore flicked the ball over a defender and retrieved it, then lined a shot into the upper left corner. “The immediate feeling was relief,” Horrocks said. “It was a culmination of three hard months, and we were finally able to take a breath. Then our thoughts went to how proud we are of the girls, and how awesome this was.” The players rushed to mob goalkeeper Stella Siller, then dashed toward the stands, hopping a fence to hug their parents and fans who made the 400-mile trip to support them. “Coming into this season, the outside expectations were incredibly high based on how we performed last year, but the level of difficulty had increased,” assistant coach Paxton Ballard said. “The roster had changed, we dealt with setbacks, and the cards were stacked against us. item.title: Dolphins Defense Shines While Malik Willis Struggles With Injury
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins defense finally found its rhythm on Sunday, yet the offense could not keep up. Detroit managed only 19 points and 4.6 yards per play against a unit that had struggled all year. The Lions usually average 29 points per game, but they only were able to score 1 touchdown against this Miami squad. Rookie Chris Johnson even grabbed an interception while the run defense held Jahmyr Gibbs to just 74 yards. Despite the strong defensive showing, the loss to the Lions leaves the team at 1-7. The offense sputtered as quarterback Malik Willis looked slow and hesitant on the field. He had two scrambles for only 7 yards, a stark contrast to his usual dynamic play with his legs. Willis has been dealing with a groin injury for weeks, and his movement clearly suffered during the game. The team faces a tough road ahead as they try to find their identity. Defense Steps Up in a Big Way The defensive unit did everything asked of them against a potent Detroit offense. Jared Goff was limited to 6.8 yards per attempt and did not throw a single touchdown pass. This was the first time all season the pass defense allowed a completion percentage below 70 percent. Safety Dante Trader Jr. explained that the coaches emphasized disguising coverages to confuse the quarterback. The plan worked well enough to hold the league’s high-scoring Lions under their typical output. Trader noted that the team is still figuring out exactly who they are on that side of the ball. He feels the defense is trying to become physical while limiting explosive plays. The coaching staff wants to see if they can stick to that identity against tougher teams. The effort was there, but the result on the scoreboard did not reflect the hard work put in by the players. Willis Struggles as Rebuild Continues Head coach Jeff Hafley admitted that Willis had issues with mobility during the game against Detroit. The protection broke down at times, but Willis also lacked the speed to escape the pocket and run. This marks a shift from his earlier performances where he used his legs to make big plays. The injury report lists him with a groin issue, and his reluctance to run is a major concern for the offense. The team is in the middle of a dramatic rebuild with the youngest roster in the NFL. Veteran linebacker Jordyn Brooks calls the situation “Optimistic and hopeful” despite the poor record. Coach Hafley says there is “a lot that I’m really encouraged by” regarding the young players. Yet the hard truth remains that the team is struggling to produce points consistently. Midseason grades from Yahoo Sports highlight that the Dolphins are 30th in the league for on-target passes. item.description: Motorsport photo Turner Motorsport is set to celebrate a milestone 30th season of professional racing in 2027, renewing its long-standing exclusivity with BMW and welcoming a familiar face back to its full-time driver lineup. The New Hampshire-based squad will anchor its 2027 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship campaign around the #96 BMW M4 GT3 EVO in the GTD class, anchored by full-season co-drivers Robby Foley and Jake Walker. Walker returns to the Turner fold after serving as the team's IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup driver in 2024 and 2025. During his initial stint, Walker impressed with a second-place podium finish at Indianapolis Motor Speedway in 2024 to aid Turner’s second-place finish in the GTD championship, followed by a team-best fifth-place finish at the Rolex 24 At Daytona in 2025. He also scored nine wins to finish runner-up in the IMSA VP Racing SportsCar Challenge GTDX championship that same year. "I’m really excited to be back with Turner Motorsport and BMW Motorsport for the 2027 season," Walker said, noting the confidence he brings into his full-time return. "I’ve learned a tremendous amount as a driver during my first full-time IMSA season, and I’m excited to bring that experience back to the team. I have a lot of confidence in the people around me, and I’m looking forward to getting to work and seeing what we can accomplish together." #96 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT3 EVO: Robby Foley, Patrick Gallagher, Jake Walker, Jens Klingmann #96 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT3 EVO: Robby Foley, Patrick Gallagher, Jake Walker, Jens Klingmann Team owner Will Turner highlighted Walker’s growth as a key factor in bringing him back alongside Foley for a complete championship run. For Foley, 2027 marks his 10th season with Turner Motorsport and ninth full-time campaign in GTD. The BMW M Works driver – who acts as both a lead competitor and a mentor for younger talent within the team's driver pipeline – comes off a strong campaign where he clinched his fourth title under the Turner banner by winning the Indianapolis 8 Hour and securing the Pro championship in GT World Challenge America, alongside a second-place finish in IMSA GTD. item.title: Jets might've missed a huge opportunity amid Jaguars trade interest in Will McDonald Iv
item.description: Jets might've missed a huge opportunity amid Jaguars trade interest in Will McDonald Iv originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets have not made a significant trade before the 2026 NFL trade deadline yet. They sent Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a sixth-round pick, which is a solid deal for a poor 2-7 Jets team. While Breece Hall and Garrett Wilson have popped up in trade rumors, neither is likely to go. The same cannot be said for edge rusher Will McDonald IV. He's been mentioned in trade rumors, but the Jets have made it clear they want to keep the 27-year-old edge. However, that might've been a big mistake, as the report from Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer on McDonald revealed the Jacksonville Jaguars made a "significant" offer for McDonald that the Jets maybe should've taken considering the moves the Jaguars made. Jets might've missed chance to land haul from Jaguars for Will McDonald IV "The trade request of Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV is interesting," Breer writes. "The Jaguars, before the flurry of action on Monday, had made a significant offer for him." Unfortunately for the Jets, that significant trade offer might now be off the table. The reason why? The Jaguars made two massive moves on Monday. They sent a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III, and then the Jaguars sent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis. Those were two massive moves for the Jaguars, and trades that could be seen as overpays. If the Jaguars were willing to spend so much on Bates and Davis, it would stand to reason that they would've offered a lot for McDonald. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade While there's not been any confirmed reporting on what the Jaguars "significant" trade offer for McDonald was, if it was equal to or more than a third-round pick, this might've been a huge missed opportunity for the Jets. McDonald requested a trade, which would indicate his time with the team might be coming to an end. Instead of trading him, the Jets have pushed the narrative that he's a key piece of their defense going forward. However, with a chance to get a significant return from the Jaguars on the table, the Jets didn't take it based on the Jaguars' trades for Davis and Bates, and now such an offer might not be in play. It's too soon to say the Jets made a massive mistake, but there's no denying that this was a missed opportunity to get a likely very strong haul for McDonald after the edge rusher requested a trade.
